title: Total unimodularity of the incidence matrix characterizes bipartiteness
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $M$ be its vertex–edge incidence matrix over $\bbz$, whose entry in row $v$ and column $e$ is $1$ when $v$ is an endpoint of the edge $e$ and $0$ otherwise. Then $M$ is totally unimodular — that is, every square submatrix of $M$ has determinant $-1$, $0$, or $1$ — if and only if $G$ is bipartite.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
M is the integer vertex-edge incidence matrix of G
replaced:
\emph{The incidence matrix of a simple graph \texttt{G} is totally
unimodular if and only if \texttt{G} is bipartite.}
